guard: a manager that may no longer serve detaches its agents — it does not stop them and does not make their footprint deprovisionable — while the ordinary shutdown path stays destructive
why: NO BUILD IN `command`, AND THAT IS A CLAIM THIS RUN CHECKS RATHER THAN ASSUMES. The suite
imports the subject RELATIVELY (`../src/manager.js`), so tsx loads `manager.ts` itself and a
mutation on it is live with no `dist` in the path. `@cotal-ai/core` is imported for TYPES only
and every plane the cells touch is stubbed, so no built artifact sits between the mutation and
the run. If that were wrong, mutation 1 would come back SURVIVED — it restores the whole defect
— so the load path is PROVEN by the run rather than asserted here.
MUTATION 1 IS THE DEFECT VERBATIM, not an approximation: the two-branch teardown that shipped.
It is the reason this suite exists. It must kill on the `does not stop child` cells.
MUTATION 2 IS THE CARELESS EDIT, and it is the one that matters most. The detach still detaches
and still does not stop anything — every cell about the CHILD stays green — but the agent leaves
the map without the flag every deprovision call site filters on, so its credential and durables
become selectable for teardown by any concurrent path. A change that looks correct from the
child's side and silently revokes the footprint is exactly the regression this pins.
MUTATION 3 DELETES THE ANNOUNCEMENT. The manager stays CORRECT and the operator goes blind.
That is not hypothetical here: the incident that motivated this lane could not be attributed
precisely because the manager logs nothing when seats leave its ownership. A silent detach is
indistinguishable at the console from the teardown it replaced.
MUTATION 4 IS THE CONTROL AND ALSO A REAL INVARIANT, which is why it is not a throwaway. It
makes the ORDINARY shutdown path detach too. Every lease-loss cell stays green — the change
under test is untouched — and only the control cell reddens. It therefore proves two separate
things at once: that the `stops` counter fires (so the zeros in the graded cells are earned and
not the reading of a dead instrument), and that `cotal down` / Ctrl-C stay destructive. Leaving
twelve agents running after an operator asked for a shutdown is the opposite failure to the one
this lane fixes, and nothing else in the suite would catch it.
MUTATION 5 PINS THE OWNERSHIP RELEASE, which the fix did not change and which no graded cell
would otherwise defend. An agent left in the map after the process has decided to exit is owned
by a manager that is going away, and a later path in the same process could still act on it.
NOT GRADED, and said rather than implied: that a detached child actually SURVIVES. It does not,
for the pty runtime — measured separately, a `@lydell/node-pty` child dies when its spawning
process exits, with a passing positive control on the same instrument — and no mutation here
could show otherwise, because these cells use a fake handle and never start a process. The
survival half belongs to the seat-host slice. A mutation aimed at it would report SURVIVED and
read as a coverage gap rather than as the out-of-scope boundary it is.
MUTATION 6 IS THE FIRST CUT OF THIS FIX, kept because it is the mistake the next person makes.
Detach is right for a manager that may no longer SERVE and wrong while a maintenance cut has
committed and not finalized: that inventory is still owed a replay, and a successor replaying it
over live children spawns a second copy of every seat under the same identities. The unconditional
detach passed every cell in this suite as first written and was caught by `smoke:preserve-state`;
cell 4 and this mutation bring that boundary inside this suite so it is defended from both sides.

mutations.name: the defect restored: lease loss tears the managed agents down instead of detaching them
mutations.find:
if (this.maintenanceState === "active" && !this.resumeRequired) this.detachManagedAgents(`lease loss: ${proof}`);
      else await this.stopRetainedAgentsOnExit();
mutations.replace:
if (this.maintenanceState === "active" && !this.resumeRequired) await this.teardownManagedAgents();
      else await this.stopRetainedAgentsOnExit();
mutations.expectRed: lease loss does not stop child 1
mutations.cell: lease loss does not stop child 1
mutations.note: The shipped branch, restored exactly. A supervisor that lost its lease hard-stops every seat and deprovisions its credential — the behaviour that made a broker timeout cost twelve agents.

mutations.name: the retention flag is dropped, so the children live and their footprint becomes deprovisionable
mutations.expectRed: lease loss marks the agent retained rather than deprovisionable
mutations.cell: lease loss marks the agent retained rather than deprovisionable
mutations.note: The half fix. Nothing stops a child, so every child-side cell stays green; only the flag that keeps a deprovision call site from selecting the agent is gone.

mutations.name: the detach is silent: correct behaviour, blind operator
mutations.expectRed: lease loss logs a detach line naming the seat
mutations.cell: lease loss logs a detach line naming the seat
mutations.note: A careless edit, not a malicious one. The manager does the right thing and says nothing about it, which is the state the motivating incident was diagnosed in.

mutations.name: CONTROL and invariant: the ordinary shutdown path detaches too, so Ctrl-C leaves every agent running
mutations.find: await this.teardownManagedAgents(); // normal shutdown stays destructive (#159 B2)
mutations.expectRed: CONTROL: the ordinary stop path stops the child
mutations.cell: CONTROL: the ordinary stop path stops the child (instrument fires)
mutations.note: Doubles as the positive control for the `stops` counter and as the guard on the opposite failure: an operator who asked for a shutdown must get one.

mutations.name: the detached agents stay in the managed map, owned by a manager that is exiting
mutations.expectRed: lease loss releases ownership of the agent
mutations.cell: lease loss releases ownership of the agent (this instance stops managing it)
mutations.note: Not changed by the fix and not defended by any other cell: ownership release is what stops a later path in this same process from acting on a seat this instance has given up.

mutations.name: the two arms are collapsed: a resume-pending cut detaches too, so a successor replays its inventory over live children
mutations.find:
if (this.maintenanceState === "active" && !this.resumeRequired) this.detachManagedAgents(`lease loss: ${proof}`);
      else await this.stopRetainedAgentsOnExit();
mutations.expectRed: a resume-pending cut still stops its children on lease loss
mutations.cell: a resume-pending cut still stops its children on lease loss (never detaches them)
mutations.note: The first cut of this fix, verbatim. It detached unconditionally, which `smoke:preserve-state` caught: a committed-not-finalized inventory is still owed a replay, and children left running are spawned a second time under the same identities.
